answer: An agent network curbs Sybil attacks via distributed acoustic time-of-flight verification. Nodes prove distinct physical positions by timestamping unforgeable ambient transients, like a raven call echoing through standing timber, using a microphone focused by a parabolic mirror. Forging identities forces an attacker to deploy discrete physical sensor hardware across real terrain. However, wind shear and thermal gradients perturb acoustic propagation, periodically rejecting legitimate nodes.
